# build_game_json_files

[← Command index](README.md)

Create or update the JSON file of each game found in a locker.

## Synopsis

```
build_game_json_files [options]
```

## Description

Lists the game folders in the locker for the selected categories and, for each one,
creates its JSON file in the game metadata repository if missing, then fills it from
the game's files: the file list (with real names when the locker is encrypted), the
DLC, update, extra and dependency files kept in those subfolders, the most likely
launch or transform file, and for store games the store's latest app data.

JSON files live under `Json/<supercategory>/<category>/<subcategory>/` in the metadata
repository, with an extra first-letter folder on platforms that use one. Values that
are filled once are kept when already present, so re-running updates rather than
replaces a file. Only the `Roms`, `DLC` and `Updates` supercategories have JSON files.

The game directory is `-i` if given, otherwise the game's place under `-b`, otherwise
the gaming folder of the `-l` locker (the Local locker when `-l` is omitted).

## Options

### Input

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Directory holding the game's files, used instead of the locker directory. |

### Selection

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-u, --game_supercategory <game_supercategory>` | Supercategory of the games to build. Default: `Roms`. Allowed: `Assets`, `Emulators`, `Roms`, `DLC`, `Updates`, `Tags`, `Saves`, `Setup`, `Installs`. |
| `-c, --game_category <game_category>` | Category of the games to build; all categories when omitted. Allowed: `Computer`, `Microsoft`, `Nintendo`, `Other`, `Sony`. |

PlayStation 3`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation 4`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Portable`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Portable Minis`, `Sony PlayStation Network - PlayStation Vita`, `Sony PlayStation Portable`, `Sony PlayStation Portable Video`, `Sony PlayStation Vita`. |
| `-n, --game_name <game_name>` | Build only the game with this exact folder name; every game in the locker when omitted. |

## Examples

### Build JSON for one new update from the local locker

```bash
build_game_json_files -u Updates -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -n "Pokemon Legends Z-A (World)" -l Local
```

### Build JSON for a whole platform from a remote locker

```bash
build_game_json_files -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -l Hetzner
```

### Build JSON for all DLC

```bash
build_game_json_files -u DLC -l Local
```

### Build one game's JSON from files in another directory

```bash
build_game_json_files -i /path/to/game/files -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -n "Game Name" -l Local
```

### Show what would be built without writing

```bash
build_game_json_files -c Nintendo -s "Nintendo Switch" -l Local -p -v
```

## Notes

- Run this for a game newly added to a locker when `upload_game_files` reports that it cannot find the game's JSON file.
- `-n` must name a game folder that exists in the locker; games are always listed from the locker, even with `-i`.
- `-i` is used as the directory of every selected game, so use it together with `-n`.
- The supercategory defaults to `Roms`; pass `-u` for DLC or updates.
